content.value_statement: Competitor traffic data can be difficult to compare across sources. This skill gathers paid traffic and SEO estimates into a comparison and identifies growth opportunities.
actual_capabilities: Discover organic search competitors and retrieve target traffic trends.
Screen candidate domains using estimated monthly visits.
Compare traffic channels, trends, backlinks, domain ratings, and keyword metrics.
Retrieve leading organic keywords and landing page URLs.
Quote batches, apply spending limits, and report actual charges.
Save request plans, raw results, and English or Chinese summaries.
limitations: Requires the AIsa CLI, a signed-in account, and paid access for data calls.
A paid run proceeds after quoting without a separate approval prompt.
Similarweb measures whole domains, not individual site sections.
Keyword results are limited, and regional Semrush estimates differ from worldwide Similarweb estimates.

use_cases.title: Compare direct competitors
use_cases.description: Compare traffic sources and SEO metrics across a target and selected rival domains.

use_cases.title: Find search opportunities
use_cases.description: Review leading competitor keywords and landing pages to identify content opportunities.

use_cases.title: Screen a market
use_cases.description: Discover and screen candidate sites before selecting a smaller group for detailed analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Discover competitors
prompt_templates.prompt: Discover organic competitors for [domain] and quote the research before running paid calls.

prompt_templates.title: Screen candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Screen [domain list] by monthly visits for [month]. Show the quote before any paid run.

prompt_templates.title: Compare traffic
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [target domain] with [competitor domains] for [month]. Include traffic channels, trends, backlinks, and data caveats.

prompt_templates.title: Develop opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [target domain] and [competitor domains]. Compare traffic and keywords, then propose three opportunities supported by observed metrics and report costs.

output_examples.input: Compare example.com with competitor.example for the latest full month.
output_examples.output: A comparison table shows estimated visits, channel shares, search metrics, and domain ratings. The report states the quote, charges, and data limitations.
A keyword table lists available search terms, positions, monthly volumes, and landing pages. The report notes that the results are not a complete keyword list.

best_practices: Review the quote and approve the budget before initiating a paid run.
Use the latest complete month and specify relevant competitor domains.
Check regional coverage and source differences before interpreting estimates.
anti_patterns: Treat traffic estimates as exact analytics measurements.
Run paid batches without reviewing expected costs.
Assume domain-wide traffic isolates a specific product or site section.

faq.question: What does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires the AIsa CLI and a signed-in account. Paid data calls may incur charges.

faq.question: Does it quote costs first?
faq.answer: Yes. The script quotes each batch, but a run with --run continues without a separate confirmation prompt.

faq.question: Which data sources are used?
faq.answer: The workflow uses Similarweb traffic data, Semrush search data, and Ahrefs domain ratings through AIsa.

faq.question: Can it measure traffic to a site section?
faq.answer: Similarweb queries cover whole domains. A page-level Semrush keyword query may provide a limited alternative.

faq.question: Are keyword results complete?
faq.answer: No. The documented keyword response contains approximately the leading 20 rows.

faq.question: Where are results saved?
faq.answer: The script saves request plans, raw results, and a Markdown summary in the selected output directory.
